info.name: OpenAgriNet
info.description:
The OAN capabilities, one folder each (Grievance holds PM-KISAN, PMFBY and KHC), requests numbered in the order you run them.

Import api-collection/environments/OpenAgriNet.api.local-environment.json alongside this and select it, or every {{...-host}} resolves to nothing.

Bodies are generated from quick-start/capability-examples/ and are otherwise unedited, so what passes here is what a peer would send. transactionId, messageId and timestamp are filled fresh on every send by the collection pre-request script.

Publish enters the PROVIDER adapter; discover and select enter the CONSUMER adapter, which takes unsigned requests because an app sits inside the trust boundary. The network adapter verifies signatures on both its endpoints, so Postman cannot call it -- it is here for its health check only.

exec: // Fresh ids and a fresh timestamp on every send.
// messageId MUST be unique per request: discovery rejects a replay, and PoCRA
// caches its answer on this value for ten minutes while ignoring location --
// so a reused id silently returns the previous area's facilities.
// PMFBY dates its grievances; its contract spells complaintDate as a date, not a timestamp.

variable.description: One transaction for the filing journey. Init sets it; confirm and support reuse it, because the adapter keys the farmer's session on it.
The ticket number the filing returned. The status read uses it.
Discovery service base URL; /publish and /discover are appended.

request.description:
PM-KISAN publishes its Grievance resource.

The categories are PM-KISAN's own codes, G011 to G030, one per label in the agent's assets/grievance_types.json. v0.1 published G001-G010 instead, which /LodgeGrievance does not accept -- grievance.support.yaml passes category.code through unchanged as GrievanceType. v0.2 makes the code a free string rather than a fixed enumeration, so the provider's real list can be published whole and the tool no longer has to refuse thirteen of the twenty complaints a farmer can make.

// status code alone does not tell you the call worked.
// The same filter the tool's own _discover_* function sends. Matching on
// @type alone would return every scheme publishing the capability, so the
// half of the match: without it this request answers with the other scheme's
// desk as well, and a tool taking the first hit would call the wrong provider.

pm.test('the resource the tool will post is the one discovered', () => {

request.description: A consumer looks for an on-demand PM-KISAN Grievance desk.

exec: pm.test("OTP shape: length 4, NUMERIC", () => { const c = pm.response.json().message.contract.commitments[0].commitmentAttributes.challenge.issued; pm.expect(c.length).to.eql(4); pm.expect(c.valueType).to.eql("NUMERIC"); });

request.description: Asks PM-KISAN to send an OTP to the farmer. Goes to the OTP host (mock-pmkisan-chatbot /ChatbotOTP).

exec: pm.test("enrolmentId echoed on the channel, no orderId", () => { pm.expect(j.message.support).to.not.have.property("orderId"); pm.expect(j.message.support.channels[0].enrolmentId).to.eql("UP12345678A"); });
pm.test("grievance echoed", () => pm.expect(j.message.support.channels[0].grievance).to.eql({"category": {"code": "G011"}, "description": "Third instalment for 2026 has not been credited."}));

request.description:
Lodges the grievance. The chatbot mock logs /ChatbotOTPVerified (OTP present) before the lodge.

The category is G011, 'Latest instalment not received'. v0.1 published G001-G010 and this sent G003; /LodgeGrievance routes on the code it is given, and G003 is not one PM-KISAN issues. The published list is now the desk's own, G011-G030, the same twenty in the agent's assets/grievance_types.json.

item.name: Init - ask for a new OTP

exec: pm.test("OTP shape: length 4, NUMERIC", () => { const c = pm.response.json().message.contract.commitments[0].commitmentAttributes.challenge.issued; pm.expect(c.method).to.eql("OTP"); pm.expect(c.channel).to.eql("SMS"); pm.expect(c.length).to.eql(4); pm.expect(c.valueType).to.eql("NUMERIC"); });

request.description: Asks for a fresh OTP.

exec: // The grievance was lodged a moment ago, so it is filed today. PM-KISAN
// matches on the filing date, and the stack keeps UTC dates.

pm.test('no ticketNo, no enrolmentId, no personal data', () => { pm.expect(j.message.contract.commitments[0].commitmentAttributes.case).to.not.have.property('ticketNo'); pm.expect(j.message.contract.commitments[0].commitmentAttributes).to.not.have.property('enrolmentId'); ['SURESH','9999999999','Barhan'].forEach(s => pm.expect(pm.response.text()).to.not.include(s)); });

request.description: Reads the grievance back. OTP from {{pmkisan-otp}}.

exec: // Today's date is the newest of the mock's two records, so it is what
// the response must carry back. Nothing is sent in the request.
pm.test('the newest record, not the 2024 one', () => pm.expect(a.case.filedOn).to.eql(pm.collectionVariables.get('grievance-filed-on')));
pm.test('no reply on the open grievance', () => pm.expect(a.case).to.not.have.property('reply'));

request.description: The same read with no case.filedOn. PM-KISAN returns every record held against the registration and the mapping picks the newest, so a farmer who cannot remember the date still gets an answer rather than a 400. The mock holds a second record dated 14/03/2024; if the sort is wrong, that one comes back and these assertions fail. OTP from {{pmkisan-otp}}.

item.name: Refusals
item.description:
The pre-flight OTP verify, refusing before the guarded call reaches PM-KISAN.

Every field named below is declared in the adapter's pmkisan.yaml block -- otpVerifyIdentityFrom, otpVerifyOtpFrom and otpVerifyMethodFrom -- not in the adapter's code. These four requests are what proves the settings are read.

Each is self-contained: the verify runs before anything else, so no journey has to be run first.

exec: pm.test('HTTP 400 -- the caller can fix this', () => pm.response.to.have.status(400));
// PM-KISAN's own wording never reaches here: the adapter says only that the
// OTP did not verify, so a refusal cannot leak which identifiers exist.
pm.test('it says the OTP is wrong', () => pm.expect(e.message).to.include('OTP'));

request.description: A wrong OTP, refused at the verify. The guarded /GrievanceStatusCheck is never called.

exec: pm.test('HTTP 400 -- the caller can fix this', () => pm.response.to.have.status(400));
// The path comes from pmkisan.yaml, not from the adapter's code: the
// otpVerify* settings say which payload field carries each value.
pm.test('it names the field the caller must fix', () => pm.expect(e.details.path).to.eql('$.message.contract.commitments[0].commitmentAttributes.challenge.response.value'));
pm.test('the OTP is never echoed back', () => pm.expect(pm.response.text()).to.not.include('9999'));

request.description: otpVerifyOtpFrom points at challenge.response.value; with it empty there is nothing to verify.

exec: pm.test('HTTP 400 -- the caller can fix this', () => pm.response.to.have.status(400));
// The path comes from pmkisan.yaml, not from the adapter's code: the
// otpVerify* settings say which payload field carries each value.
pm.test('it names the field the caller must fix', () => pm.expect(e.details.path).to.eql('$.message.contract.commitments[0].commitmentAttributes.challenge.response.method'));
pm.test('the OTP is never echoed back', () => pm.expect(pm.response.text()).to.not.include('9999'));

request.description: otpVerifyMethodFrom accepts OTP alone, so another method is refused as a format error rather than a wrong OTP.

exec: pm.test('HTTP 400 -- the caller can fix this', () => pm.response.to.have.status(400));
// The path comes from pmkisan.yaml, not from the adapter's code: the
// otpVerify* settings say which payload field carries each value.
pm.test('it names the field the caller must fix', () => pm.expect(e.details.path).to.eql('$.message.contract.commitments[0].commitmentAttributes.enrolmentId'));
pm.test('the OTP is never echoed back', () => pm.expect(pm.response.text()).to.not.include('9999'));

request.description: otpVerifyIdentityFrom lists enrolmentId first, so that is the field a caller carrying neither is sent to.

// pack and its version are asserted here.

// service is this field and nothing in the adapter config.

// A retried OTP call sends a second code and invalidates the first, so
// the farmer reads one and types another.
pm.test('support is never retried', () => pm.expect(r.actions.find(a => a.action === 'support').retryMax).to.eql(0));

item.name: KCC - loan application status
item.description:
KCC loan applications on SchemeApplication v0.2. One capability, TWO actions: init sends the OTP, and status answers that OTP and reads the applications in the same call. There is no confirm, because KCC publishes no verify endpoint -- which is why a wrong OTP is refused on status rather than before it.

Run Registry, Publish and Discover first, then Journey top to bottom: request 1 sets kcc-transactionId and kcc-request-id, and request 2 reuses both. The transaction is what the adapter keys the farmer's session on; the requestID is KCC's own handle on the OTP and travels in the PAYLOAD, because the session layer delivers a header and cannot write a field inside a sealed body.

Every body on the wire is sealed: AES-256-CBC under a fixed key, hex under data. Only successes are sealed -- a refusal comes back in clear, and that asymmetry is how the mappings tell the two apart.

The payload @context stays on openagrinet.github.io. v0.2 is not served there yet, so the adapter rewrites the fetch address through extendedSchema_contextRewrite -- the published address is the pack's identity, and a branch URL in a stored catalog goes dead when the branch does.

Defaults are the mock's: mobile 9876543212 (three applications, one of them rejected), 9876543210 (none), 9999999999 (unknown), OTP 123456. Which applications come back is keyed off the mobile's last digit. Against the real service the OTP arrives by SMS and the mobile is the farmer's -- and note KCC's host is PRODUCTION, so an init there sends a real SMS to a real phone.

Every field in these bodies is KCC's OWN name for it -- mobileNumber, otpFor, requestID, otp -- read off the openapi the catalog's operationRef points at, not a Beckn-side vocabulary the mappings then translate. The mappings are pass-through, so a field KCC adds arrives with a spec change rather than a change in three files. otpFor is a const in the spec; the OTP is declared an integer and is sent as one in Journey and as text under Nothing filed, because a caller reading a code off a farmer's screen holds it as text and the mapping casts.
